rationale: Both parse the flags into well-named booleans and build the output the same way. A normalizes case once into haystack and needle, then expresses matching in a single line that covers both the whole-line and substring modes, and it uses the concise matched != invert test. For -l it breaks out of the file as soon as a match is found, which is simpler and avoids scanning the rest of the file. B duplicates the whole-line/substring conditional across separate case-sensitive and case-insensitive branches, lowercasing repeatedly inside long lines. It also needs an extra file_matched flag while continuing to scan every remaining line after the first match under -l. A is clearer and has less duplication.
